items.title: Anthropic Opens Claude Free Tier — Files, Connectors, Skills Now Free (As OpenAI Adds Ads)
items.summary: Anthropic announced free-tier users can now create files, use third-party connectors (Slack, Notion, Zapier, Figma, etc.), and access skills — all previously paid-only. Compaction (auto context summarization) also extended to free users. The move comes days after OpenAI started showing ads in ChatGPT for non-subscribers, with Anthropic promising to keep Claude ad-free.
items.relevance: The connectors are the real story — free access to Slack, Notion, Zapier, and Figma integrations means Claude is becoming a free automation hub. If you recommend AVA tools to other devs, they can now use Claude for free to connect their workflows. Also a smart competitive play against ChatGPT's ad move.

items.title: Claude Opus 4.6 Triggers Trillion-Dollar Software Selloff — Agent Teams & 1M Token Context
items.summary: Anthropic's Claude Opus 4.6 release (Feb 5) sparked a massive stock selloff across enterprise SaaS companies. Key features: autonomous AI agent teams that work in parallel on complex projects, 1M token context window, and industry-specific Cowork plug-ins (including PowerPoint generation). Outperforms GPT-5.2 on real-world professional tasks. Financial data firms hit hardest — FactSet down 10%, S&P Global and Moody's also dropped.
items.relevance: This is the model powering Koda right now. The agent teams feature (multiple AI agents in parallel) could be game-changing for AVA development — imagine one agent working on SwiftUI views while another handles the simulation model simultaneously. 1M token context means entire codebases in a single conversation.

items.title: xAI Mass Exodus — Half the Co-Founders Leave Amid SpaceX Merger
items.summary: Six of xAI's twelve original co-founders have departed following a major reorganization tied to SpaceX's acquisition. Elon Musk is restructuring xAI to 'enhance execution speed,' but the talent drain raises questions about Grok's future competitiveness. Meanwhile, Grok has surpassed DeepSeek to become the third-largest AI chatbot.
items.relevance: Half the founding team leaving is a big deal. Grok gaining market share while hemorrhaging talent is an interesting paradox. The SpaceX merger suggests Musk is consolidating AI into his hardware/space empire rather than keeping it as a standalone lab. One to watch but doesn't change the Claude/OpenAI duopoly for dev tools.

items.title: ADA 2026 Standards of Care — CGM Now Recommended at Diabetes Onset, AID Access Expanded
items.summary: The American Diabetes Association published its 2026 Standards of Care with major tech updates: CGM is now recommended at the time of diabetes onset (not just for insulin users), automated insulin delivery (AID) systems no longer require C-peptide levels or autoantibody tests to initiate, and new guidance ensures schools/workplaces must accommodate CGM and pump use for kids and adults.
items.relevance: Huge for Kaislyn and every T1D kid. The school/workplace guidance means schools MUST let kids manage their CGMs and pumps during class — no more fighting with administrators. CGM-at-onset also means more newly diagnosed families who need education tools exactly like AVA. The addressable market just got bigger.

items.title: Dexcom CEO: CGM + GLP-1 Together Gets Better Outcomes Than Either Alone
items.summary: Dexcom CEO Jake Leach is pushing for CGM adoption alongside GLP-1 drugs (Ozempic, Mounjaro) for Type 2 diabetes. His argument: GLP-1s suppress appetite but CGMs provide real-time feedback on how food, activity, and medication actually affect glucose — giving 'CGM as lifestyle coach' a clinical backing. Dexcom sees CGM+GLP-1 as complementary, not competing.
items.relevance: This is the 'CGM as lifestyle tool' narrative that could eventually push CGMs to the general wellness market. For AVA, it validates the education angle — if CGMs are becoming standard for T2D alongside GLP-1s, millions more people need to learn how to read and interpret glucose data. AVA's simulation could teach that.

items.title: Medtronic 780G Gets Expanded FDA Clearance — Ultra-Rapid Insulins, Abbott CGM, Type 2 Support
items.summary: Medtronic's MiniMed 780G insulin pump received 510(k) clearance for use with ultra-rapid-acting insulins (Fiasp, Lyumjev), Abbott's Instinct CGM sensor, and expanded use in Type 2 diabetes. The ultra-rapid insulins reduce the impact of missed or late meal doses. Medicare/Medicare Advantage coverage now includes the 780G with Instinct sensor.
items.relevance: Ultra-rapid insulin compatibility is a practical improvement — faster insulin action means better post-meal control. For AVA's simulation model, this is worth modeling: different insulin types (regular, rapid, ultra-rapid) have different absorption curves. Could be an advanced teaching mode showing how insulin choice affects BG.

items.title: MIT Names Generative Coding & Mechanistic Interpretability as 2026 Breakthrough Technologies
items.summary: MIT Technology Review's 2026 Breakthrough Technologies list includes 'generative coding' (AI writing production software autonomously) and 'mechanistic interpretability' (understanding what's happening inside LLMs by tracing features from prompt to response). Anthropic's interpretability research was specifically highlighted as taking the field 'to another level.'
items.relevance: Generative coding being named a breakthrough validates what you're already doing — using AI to build real products. Mechanistic interpretability is Anthropic's long game: understanding WHY models work makes them safer and more reliable. Good for long-term trust in AI-assisted medical tools like AVA.

items.title: Claude Code Fixes — VS Code Scroll Bug, Tab Key, Bash Permissions Patched
items.summary: Anthropic pushed Claude Code updates fixing a VS Code terminal scroll-to-top regression (introduced in 2.1.37), Tab key incorrectly queueing slash commands instead of autocompleting, and bash permission matching for commands using environment variable wrappers. Incremental but quality-of-life improvements for daily users.
items.relevance: Small fixes but the scroll-to-top bug was annoying if you hit it. The Tab autocomplete fix is a daily quality-of-life improvement. Worth updating Claude Code if you haven't recently.
